description_en: Known as Cakramukteśvara, thisśivālaya, or abode of Śiva, was erected in 1894 CE (VS 1951) as a tribute to Lieutenant Cakra Śamśera, the third son of Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera.Positioned on the southern side of the Gorakhanātha temple complex in Mṛgasthalī, amidst a collection of temples reflecting the prevalent Rāṇā period architectural style, thisśivālayastands alongside the Nandabhakteśvara Mandira (PPK1955) to its east. Crafted with stone on three plinth levels, Cakramukteśvara showcases a bell-shaped roof that used to be adorned with a finial that is now (December 2023) missing. The central structure, hosting a square sanctum, is characterized by its four-sided stone entrance, each featuring an archway (toraṇa) portraying Chepu, a mythical water creature. The southern entrance is distinguished by a small Bhairava mask embedded in the wall, marking it as the primary access point to the sanctum.Inside the sanctum, Cakramukteśvara Mahādeva is venerated as the main deity in the form of a stoneśivaliṅga. A Nandī figure, Śiva's animal mount, guards the western entrance, while the usual Kāmadeva statue southeast of the temple is notably absent here. Hanging from a bell-stand south of the temple is a brass bell bearing inscriptions about the temple's construction.Despite the temple being constructed in 1894 CE (VS 1951) in memory of Lieutenant Cakra Śamśera, the individual responsible for its construction is unclear from the bell inscription. Cakra Śamśera is the third son of Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera and the first from his second wife Topakumārīdevī, a Newar from Thimi, who held the title ofŚrī3Baḍāmahārānī(the main queen) after Vīra Śamśera became prime minister (Rāja VS 2071, p.22). Married but passing away at a young age (Rāja VS 2071, p.25), the wish for Cakra Śamśera's eternal peace is evident from the temple's construction. It is, therefore, confirmed that he had already passed away by 1894 CE, during the lifetime of his father Vīra Śamśera, who himself passed away in 1901 CE (VS 1957) (Rāja VS 2071, p.21).Damaged in the 2015 earthquakes, the temple underwent restoration by the Pashupati Area Development Trust in 2019 CE (VS 2076).Daily worship for the main deity is conducted by a Brahmin from the Ḍhuṅgela caste in the mornings, with lamp offerings in the evenings, and no additional rituals are observed at this temple.
description_ne: प्रधानमन्त्री वीर शमशेरका साहिँला छोरा चक्र शमशेरको नाममा विसं १९५१ (सन् १८९४) मा चक्रमुक्तेश्वर स्थापना गरिएको थियो ।पशुपतिक्षेत्रको मृगस्थलीस्थित गोरखनाथ मन्दिरको दक्षिणतिर निर्मित यस शिवालयको पूर्वतिर नन्दभक्तेश्वर मन्दिर (PPK1955) रहेको छ । तीनतह ढुङ्गाको पेटीमाथि रहेको यो मन्दिर राणाकालमा प्रचलित शैलीमा बनाइएको छ । मन्दिरको चारैतिर ढोकाहरू रहेपनि मुख्य प्रवेशद्वार दक्षिणाभिमुख छ । हरेक ढोकामाथि ढुङ्गाको छेपु आकृति सहितको तोरण राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको अगाडि घण्टा जडान गरिएको छ भने पश्चिमपट्टिको पेटिमाथि नन्दी स्थापना गरिएको छ । यस प्रकारका मन्दिरहरूको वास्तुशैली अनुसार कामदेवको मूर्ति हुनु पर्ने स्थानमा केही देखिँदैन । घण्टाकार छानामाथिको गजूर भने हाल (डिसेम्बर २०२३) देखिँदैन ।विसं १९५१ (सन् १८९४) मा लेफटेन् जनरल चक्र शम्शेर राणाका नाममा यो मन्दिर चक्रमुक्तेश्वर स्थापना गरिएको हो । मन्दिरको घण्टमा कुँदिएको अभिलेखबाट उनका नाममा कसले यो मन्दिर स्थापना गरे भन्ने कुरा स्पष्ट हुँदैन । प्रधानमन्त्री वीर शम्शेरका साहिँला छोरा चक्र शमशेर वीरकी दोस्रो श्रीमती तोपकुमारीदेवीतर्फका जेठा छोरा हुन् । तोपकुमारीदेवी थिमिकी नेवार थिइन् र आफू प्रधानमन्त्री भए लगत्तै वीर शमशेरले उनीलाई श्री ३ बडामहारानीको पदवी दिएका थिए । विवाह गरिसकेपछि युवावस्थामै चक्र शमशेरको मृत्यू भएको थियो (Rāja VS 2071, p. 22, 25) । उनको मुक्तिको कामना गरी चक्रमुक्तेश्वरको स्थापना गरिएकाले विसं १९५१ (सन् १८९४) मा चक्र शमशेरको मृत्यू भैसकेको देखिन्छ । विसं १९५७ (सन् १९०१) मा मृत्यू भएका (Rāja VS 2071, p. 21) वीर शमशेरको जीवनकालमै छोरा चक्र शमशेरको मृत्यू भएको थियो ।विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पमा परी मन्दिर जीर्ण भएपछि पशुपति क्षेत्र विकास कोषले विसं २०७६ (सन् २०१९) मा मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो ।ढुङ्गेल थरका ब्राह्मणले यहाँ दैनिक बिहान नित्यपूजा र बेलुकी आरती गर्दै आ‍इरहेका छन् भने अन्य धार्मिक गतिविधि हुने गरेको छैन ।

historical_events.event_description: The temple built by establishing Cakramukteśvara Mahādeva in memory of Lieutenant Cakra Śamśera, the third son of Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera and the first from his second wife Topakumārīdevī. The individual responsible for its construction is, however, unclear from the bell inscription.
The Pashupati Area Development Trust carried out renovations of the temple, as it was damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.
